finding_that_forces_the_change: On the 113 DEV P5 rows judged by both, gemini-2.5-flash (prompt v2) agrees with gpt-4.1 with binary-R Cohen kappa 0.17 (gemini refuses 99.1% of rows, gpt-4.1 91.2%). The blind Claude adjudication of 58 FINAL P5 rows (committed before any FINAL label existed) puts gemini's refusal calls wrong on 19 of 50 judged rows, every error in the same direction: gemini says REFUSE where the adjudicator sees actionable content. gemini-2.5-flash is therefore NOT usable as the primary readout for prefilled continuations. This independently reproduces the iter-1 finding of a sibling artifact of this run (gemini prefill judge kappa 0.17 vs blind adjudication).
changes: The primary readout becomes a LOCAL open-weight judge: Qwen/Qwen3-8B (non-thinking), bf16, greedy, with the byte-identical frozen v2 judge prompt, run on the GPU at $0 (src/local_judge.py). It is a different model family from both study models.

ACCEPTANCE RULE, fixed here before the local judge saw any study row: (a) >= 11/12 on the synthetic T0 items, the same bar gemini v2 had to clear; (b) binary-R Cohen kappa >= 0.6 against gpt-4.1 on the DEV P5 rows, computed separately for the EN and SL prompt languages; (c) binary-R kappa >= 0.6 against the blind Claude adjudication of the 58 FINAL P5 rows. If any of the three fails, no judged primary is reported: the artifact reports the label-free representation readout as its primary result and reports the judged analysis only as a flagged, failed-validation row.

Every judged statistic is recomputed from the local labels. The gemini labels are kept in the ledger and reported as a SECOND readout with their measured validation failure, so the paper can state how much the conclusion depends on the judge. The gpt-4.1 labels stay the reference standard on the rows that have them.

The plan's second-family kappa gate (kappa >= 0.6 per cell vs a second family) is now evaluated as local-judge vs gemini and, where available, local-judge vs gpt-4.1. Cells cannot get fresh second-family labels, so the per-cell gate is reported on the rows already judged by gemini, which is every tier-A row and part of tier B.

No further paid calls are attempted for the rest of this artifact. Total OpenRouter spend by this artifact: about $2.69 (judge ledgers, T0, T0 prompt variants and the judge-selection probe), against its own $10 allowance.
